title: Please implement a cookie banner blocker that works like "I don't care about cookies"
body:
Please implement a cookie banner blocker that works like "I don't care about cookies"
Official Website: https://www.i-dont-care-about-cookies.eu/
I think the consent policy for installing cookies is also really nice. 
Look here: https://www.i-dont-care-about-cookies.eu/notices/3.0.2/
and here: https://www.i-dont-care-about-cookies.eu/cookie-installing-permission-header/
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: `I don't care about cookies` isn't that optimised. But it would be handy to block cookie notices as an option.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
I don't know, if it's optimized or not, but in my experience especially the chrome extension works really well! The best thing about this extension is, that I do not have to make script blocking in brave to the default (to block all cookie notices), because it just destroys most of the websites I visit.

BTW: this chrome extension is available under GPL 3.0 as stated inside the license-file in the extension-folder.

comments.author: Participant 5
comments.body:
@RichyHBM the list is being shipped on Android currently.  So right now the network half of the list should be applied in all versions of the android browser.  

The brave android browser doesn't currently apply cosmetic rules though, the way the desktop version of Brave does.  This is bc the android version doesn't yet support extensions.  Android support for extensions is currently being worked on, and we hope to have it good to go by the end of June, 2020

comments.author: Participant 14
comments.body:
Brave just released [Blocking annoying and privacy-harming cookie consent banners](https://brave.com/privacy-updates/21-blocking-cookie-notices/). However, it works in the same way as ublock origin via a filter list ([Easylist-Cookie List - Filter Obtrusive Cookies Notice](https://easylist.to/)) and it does not work on google website (search, youtube, etc.).
In this case, an extension like [I still don't care about cookies ](https://github.com/OhMyGuus/I-Dont-Care-About-Cookies) (a fork of [I don't care about cookies](https://www.i-dont-care-about-cookies.eu/) recently acquired by avast) is still needed. Would it be possible for brave to implement something similar?

comments.author: Participant 5
comments.body:
hi @alfredonodo , let me ping @ryanbr who does most of the filter list work at Brave (and does a great job doing it).

I just wanted to note though that we decided to not go with the "I {still} don't care about cookies" approach in general because its less privacy-protecting than the filter list approach.  There are some cases though that won't work with the filter list approach (at least, not easily) for compat reasons.  This might be one of them.  We'll see what can be done using Brave's approach for the google example you mentioned and get back to you.  Thanks for raising the issue!
